[1] [3] By default, a NATS connection will echo messages if the connection also has interest in the published subject, meaning that if a publisher on a connection sends a message to a subject, any subscribers on that same connection will receive the message. To stop this behavior and ensure that messages are not delivered to subscribers on the same connection, you can opt to turn off this echo. This setting is per connection and not per application, so each connection must be configured to turn off echo. ![](../../../.gitbook/assets/noecho.svg) Keep in mind that turning echo on or off can result in a significant change to your applications communication protocol, as messages will flow or stop flowing based on this setting, and the subscribing code will not have any indication as to why.
